title: PI plan — tranche 8 (retrospective, 2026-11-28)
body:
# PI plan — tranche 8

## Objectives

O1 S06d's connector standard is accepted: web, Telegram and MCP are one connector class — one registry entry, one inbound route and grammar, one multicast dispatcher and one grant matrix — with its Phase-G review and closure complete. O2 S13's process engine is accepted and its reusable workflow catalogue is shipped (or its built claim is withdrawn): a `call` step resolves a catalogue workflow, `v1-s13-1` resolves with a commit, test and evidence, and the closed project is re-closed with its closure review. O3 S19's eval builder is accepted and stays active: evals are rows with signed-off cases, a held-out wall and an audit, its declared outputs are published, and #31's Tier-3 lane is untouched. O4 the tranche-8 exit gate exits 0 on three fresh receipts and hands a green tranche to the review that #755 records.

## Plan

Every member is one factory run, and the three packs are authored and preflighted as a set before the first write: `rework-batch.py` refuses a member whose pack fails the offline check and refuses the tranche while its demo cadence is missing. The factory executes the members in project-key order — S06d, S13, S19 — because `tranche_members` sorts by key; the WSJF ranking below is a value ordering for the review, not the execution order, and both are recorded rather than one rewritten to match the other. S19 is the only active member: its pack carries no closure keys and its receipt must leave the project `active`. S13 carries the tranche's only CODE package, so it is the one member where a green pack is not enough: the catalogue must land (or the claim be withdrawn) and `v1-s13-1` must resolve in the ledger before its receipt can be green. Tranche 8 is `planned` until #755 records the tranche-7 review, so readiness is prepared and proved gate by gate; the batch dry-run is expected to stop at the authorisation line until then.

## WSJF order

S19 — business value 8, time criticality 6, risk reduction 8, job size 8: (8+6+8)/8 = 2.75. S06d — 7, 6, 7, 8: 2.50. S13 — 9, 7, 9, 13: 1.92. The ranking is therefore S19, S06d, S13. The factory's execution order is S06d, S13, S19, the snapshot's key order; with one snapshot for all three receipts the difference changes which receipt lands first and nothing else, so the ranking is recorded for the review rather than enforced on the run. S19 leads because it is the only active member and its signed eval evidence is the acceptance bar's instrument; S13's job size is the largest because it carries the code package and a catalogue that must be authored, loaded and proved.

## Capacity and WIP

Three members, one in flight at a time. The factory is serial by construction and journals every transition, so an interrupted run resumes where it stopped. One live-record writer (this session), one build concurrency (the binary is already built for schema 110; the pack work needs no compile), and at most two open batches. The tranche-7 session prepares on the same replay record with distinct rows; tranche 8's snapshot is pinned separately and re-pinned only if a member row changes.

## Evidence

The pinned snapshot (its manifest sha256 is recorded in the tranche-8 evidence directory), `docs/evidence/rework-register.json` (38 open packages on the three members (S06d 13, S13 14, S19 11)), the ledger finding `v1-s13-1`, the acceptance manifests `acceptance/programme/{S06d,S13,S19}.toml`, and the tranche-8 readiness rows written to the replay record and listed in `cadences.json`.

## Dependencies

#755 records the tranche-7 review and authorises tranche 8 (acceptance-blocked). #951 delivers tranche 7 first; S19's open question 1 blocks on S16's usage recording (`S19-eval-builder.md` §10). #31 is S19's Tier-3 lane and is related, not blocking. The seed's `depends_on`: S06d on S02/S04/S05/S06/S06b/S06c; S13 on S03/S04/S11/S15; S19 on S02/S03/S04/S06/S09/S10/S11/S16.

## Backlog refinement

The refinement reordered the seed's membership order (S06d, S13, S19) to the WSJF order S19, S06d, S13. Re-estimates: S06d — 13 open packages (2 P0, 7 P1, 4 P2); S13 — 14 open packages (2 P0, 9 P1 including the `v1-s13-1` CODE package, 3 P2); S19 — 11 open packages (2 P0, 6 P1, 3 P2), plus the tranche-level closure-output, declared-output and WBS cards the pack must discharge. The WSJF inputs are recorded in the refinement cadence's `meta.refinement.wsjf_inputs` and in `refinement-wsjf.json`.
